title: TelevisaUnivision & Fútbol de Primera Announce Exclusive Spanish-Language Radio Partnership for World Cup 2026
detail: TelevisaUnivision and Fútbol de Primera announced on May 8 an exclusive Spanish-language radio partnership covering FIFA World Cup 2026 matches across select network stations in New York, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago — four of the United States' most important Hispanic radio markets. The agreement extends Fútbol de Primera's live match commentary, analysis, and coverage to TelevisaUnivision's flagship Spanish-language radio stations in these cities, representing the largest Spanish-language radio footprint for a World Cup in US history. Three of the four covered markets (New York, Dallas, and Houston) are host-city markets: MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford/New York is home to the July 19 Final; AT&T Stadium in Dallas is the tournament's most-used venue (9 matches, including a semi-final); NRG Stadium in Houston hosts seven matches. The partnership comes as TelevisaUnivision also holds Spanish-language TV broadcast rights, making the company the dominant Spanish-language media partner for the tournament. The announcement comes 34 days before the tournament opener at Estadio Azteca.

media.caption: TelevisaUnivision and Fútbol de Primera announce exclusive Spanish-language radio partnership for World Cup 2026 in New York, Dallas, Houston, and Chicago

title: 3 Days to Provisional Squad Deadline — All 48 Nations Must Submit Player Lists to FIFA by May 11
detail: With the FIFA provisional squad submission deadline three days away on May 11, Al Jazeera published a comprehensive breakdown on May 8 of all squad announcement dates and key deadlines for the expanded 48-team tournament. All national teams are required to submit a preliminary list of 35–55 players (including a minimum of 4 goalkeepers) to FIFA by May 11; these lists are not publicly disclosed by FIFA but form the working pool for final squad selection. The club player release window begins May 25. Final 23–26-man squads must be submitted to FIFA between May 25 and June 1, with FIFA publishing all 48 final squads publicly on June 2. Key confirmed announcement dates: France on May 14 in Paris (Deschamps naming 26 players; Hugo Ekitike confirmed absent with Achilles tear); Brazil on May 18 in Rio (Ancelotti announcement; Rodrygo and Eder Militão confirmed out; Estevao status uncertain); Germany on May 21; USMNT on May 26 at The Rooftop at Pier 17 in New York City, live on FOX Sports at 3 p.m. ET. Argentina's 35-player preliminary list — expected to include Lionel Messi among 21 confirmed by Scaloni — is due May 11.

media.caption: 3 days to FIFA's provisional squad deadline — 48 nations submitting 35–55 player lists by May 11; FIFA publishes final 26-man squads June 2

title: Mbappé Hamstring Injury Raises Pre-Tournament Concern — Expected Back for El Clásico on May 10
detail: Kylian Mbappé (Real Madrid / France) suffered a hamstring injury that raised pre-tournament fitness concerns for France ahead of their squad announcement on May 14. ESPN's World Cup injury tracker reported on May 8 that Mbappé is expected to return to action for the Real Madrid vs. Barcelona El Clásico fixture scheduled for May 10 — an important signal for Deschamps, who has six days from today to finalize France's 26-man squad. France's medical staff will monitor his progress closely between now and the June 11 tournament opener. Mbappé is widely expected to be named in France's squad and lead their Group I campaign against Iraq, Senegal, and Norway. The hamstring concern comes alongside France's most significant confirmed absence: Liverpool forward Hugo Ekitike (Achilles tendon), ruled out entirely. Beyond France, the broader pre-tournament injury landscape includes: Rodrygo (Brazil) — torn ACL, out; Eder Militão (Brazil) — thigh surgery, out; Estevao (Brazil/Chelsea) — Grade 4 hamstring, status uncertain. With provisional squads due in 3 days, medical assessments across all 48 federations are at critical juncture.

media.caption: Mbappé hamstring concern ahead of May 14 France squad announcement — expected back for El Clásico May 10; Ekitike confirmed out with Achilles
